item.title: Clues about complex life come from freshly cultivated archaea
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03294-7

Two archaeal strains that belong to a lineage closely related to the ancestor of eukaryotic cells (complex cells with membrane-bound organelles) have been brought into culture. Their simple internal organization, elaborate surface structures, microbial partnerships and protein-dependent lifestyle provide clues about how eukaryotic cells arose.
item.dc:title: Clues about complex life come from freshly cultivated archaea

item.title: An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03288-5

A previously unknown mechanism required for cells to start proliferating has been identified. A combination of mathematical modelling and cell-based experiments shows that the enzyme WEE1 switches off a protein-degradation complex to allow cell proliferation to start, with implications for WEE1 inhibitors currently in trials for cancer treatments.
item.dc:title: An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors

item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03298-3

item.title: Spatial and sectoral water demand assessment for the African continent
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11199-8

Africa-wide water demand analysis across six sectors in 2020 shows that in specific regions of northern and southern Africa, the current water demand exceeds water availability.

item.title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11206-y

A multi-ancestry study of Alzheimer’s disease identifies new risk loci and potential drug targets, implicates microglia and neurons, and reveals a larger common-variant contribution than previously estimated.
item.dc:title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation

item.title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11173-4

Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling identifies cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific genetic effects that link non-coding variants to immune disease risk.

item.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11178-z

Pharmacological inhibition of the m7G methyltransferase METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and substantially prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin.
item.dc:title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers

item.title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11197-w
